Summarize Differences Between Trial Planning Objects

Source: R/class_trial_comparison.R
summary.TrialComparison.Rd

Summarizes differences between the object profiles in a trial comparison.

The TrialComparisonSummary method refreshes a summary from its underlying comparison, retaining stored display settings unless explicitly overridden. This also supports %vs% chains followed by summary(...).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'TrialComparison'
summary(
  object,
  ...,
  digits = NA_integer_,
  maxParameters = NA_integer_,
  maxProfiles = NA_integer_,
  maxObjects = NA_integer_,
  maxValues = NA_integer_,
  output = c("all", "title", "overview", "body"),
  harmonizeColumnNames = TRUE,
  textMode = c("wrap", "truncate", "full"),
  width = NA_integer_,
  showAll = NA,
  showDataType = FALSE,
  maxTableColumns = NA_integer_
)

# S3 method for class 'TrialComparisonSummary'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A TrialComparison or an existing TrialComparisonSummary.

...

Further arguments. Currently unused.

digits

Display rounding only; exact values determine differences.

maxParameters

Maximum number of differing parameters shown, across all sections. Increase this to inspect further differences.

maxProfiles

Maximum number of distinct profiles shown per parameter.

maxObjects

Maximum object numbers/names listed per profile.

maxValues

Maximum profile values shown per preview.

output

One of "all", "title", "overview", or "body".

harmonizeColumnNames

If TRUE (default), compare the harmonized columns described in getComparison(). If FALSE, compare the original parameter names, as in as.data.frame(object, harmonizeColumnNames = FALSE).

textMode

Console text handling: "wrap" (default) wraps complete text, "truncate" shows compact previews with an explicit shortening notice, and "full" writes complete text without automatic wrapping. Markdown always retains complete text in its profile tables.

width

Console line width, at least 20 characters. Defaults to getOption("width", 80L). Long unbroken words can exceed this width.

showAll

If TRUE, lift all four max* limits and disable text truncation. Wrapping remains active when textMode = "wrap". Defaults to FALSE.

showDataType

If TRUE, include data type descriptions such as integer, continuous in parameter headings. Defaults to FALSE.

maxTableColumns

Maximum result/profile columns per Markdown table block (default 4). Coordinate columns are additional. Also applies with showAll = TRUE.

Value

A TrialComparisonSummary inheriting from SummaryFactory. Its parameterInfo contains metadata, full exact profiles and object group IDs. The displayed summary is a snapshot; call summary() again after changing an underlying object. The harmonizeColumnNames attribute of parameterInfo records the selected naming mode for plotting and R-code reconstruction. Input roles take precedence when roles differ across the compared object types.

Details

Constant numeric vector cells compare equal to their scalar value regardless of vector length. Nonconstant vectors, missing values, and their positions remain part of the exact comparison. The stored comparison data are unchanged. Profile coordinates follow the parameter's source and native dimensions. Repeated design settings on simulation category rows are normalized only when the remaining coordinates uniquely determine the exact values. Stage and group domains of dimensioned parameters remain meaningful when their values are equal. Uncertain or conflicting dependencies retain additional coordinates rather than averaging or selecting an arbitrary value. Both parameter-filter options of as.data.frame.TrialComparison() use these profiles; unfiltered data-frame rows remain unchanged for plotting. This value normalization also applies when column-name harmonization is disabled. Plotting a summary retains its selected column-name mode unless custom data are supplied.

Parameter captions are resolved separately for each original object, including its design when a parameter comes from that design. parameterInfo$paramName retains the column names selected by harmonizeColumnNames; paramCaption contains the display label and paramCaptions contains captions in object order (NA for absent parameters). These captions are captured with the summary. Distinct object-specific captions are shown together and identified alongside the corresponding object labels; they do not change exact value-profile grouping. Unnamed entries are labelled Simulation when all objects are simulation results, Design when all objects are trial designs, and Result otherwise, followed by their collection position. Explicit names take precedence. Full type descriptions remain in the overview. The overview and these labels are captured with the summary. The legend explains exact profile comparison and mentions NA only when displayed profiles contain missing values. Titles distinguish designs, sample size calculations, power calculations, and power simulations. Mixed comparisons use a design plan comparison title; empty comparisons retain the general trial comparison title. Markdown output places coordinates in rows and displayed profiles in columns. Scalar profiles use one-row tables. At most maxTableColumns profile columns (default 4) appear per block, with coordinate columns repeated in each block. This layout limit also applies with showAll = TRUE. Long profile labels are listed above the tables with short references. Incompatible coordinate structures use separate tables. Missing and omitted coordinates use the same markers as console tables. Data limits apply independently of table layout.

Console output uses a single comparison line for numeric, character or logical scalar values when at most four objects are compared, all fit within the profile/object limits, captions agree and the complete line fits within width. Otherwise scalars retain the labelled profile display. Profiles with compatible coordinate columns are aligned by their exact coordinates and displayed side by side. Coordinates constant across the complete parameter are listed once, except redundant constant category types, categories and situation identifiers, which are omitted. Varying categories use an Arm or Comparison column caption where appropriate. A scalar missing profile is displayed as an NA column alongside the coordinates of the other profiles; non-missing scalars are not expanded. If the table exceeds width, values are listed vertically per coordinate. Profiles sharing at least one coordinate can use a joint table even if their remaining axes differ. A dash marks an inapplicable coordinate; values are not broadcast to categories absent from their source profile. Profiles without shared coordinates retain separate displays. <absent> denotes a coordinate absent from a profile, whereas <omitted> denotes a value outside that profile's maxValues preview. Neither marker represents a stored NA. Display choices do not change exact profile grouping.

A NULL display argument reads its setting through .getEnvironmentVariable(). Explicit arguments take precedence over environment variables, which take precedence over R options and defaults. The four default limits are 12 parameters, 3 profiles, 6 objects and 4 values. R options use the prefix rpact.comparison.summary. followed by the argument name: maxParameters, maxProfiles, maxObjects, maxValues, maxTableColumns, textMode, width, showAll or showDataType. The corresponding environment variables are RPACT_COMPARISON_SUMMARY_MAX_PARAMETERS, RPACT_COMPARISON_SUMMARY_MAX_PROFILES, RPACT_COMPARISON_SUMMARY_MAX_OBJECTS, RPACT_COMPARISON_SUMMARY_MAX_VALUES, RPACT_COMPARISON_SUMMARY_TEXT_MODE, RPACT_COMPARISON_SUMMARY_WIDTH, RPACT_COMPARISON_SUMMARY_SHOW_ALL and RPACT_COMPARISON_SUMMARY_SHOW_DATA_TYPE. Settings are captured when the summary is created. For a complete display use summary(x, showAll = TRUE); for a compact display use textMode = "truncate".
